beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Adwait Changan, and this video is about what happens when a human thinks the machine is wrong. Today we are going to learn why I built a log that refuses to settle the argument. My finance agent can be approved, rejected, or sent back. What it could not handle was a reviewer who accepts the report but rejects one number in it.

show.event: composer on cream; the fellow names himself and the subject

props.command: What happens when a reviewer accepts the report but rejects one of its findings?
output: The review gate had three answers: approve, request changes, block.
None of them fit the common case: the report is fine, that one number is not.
So disagreements are now recorded beside the finding, and neither side wins.

beats.narration_text: Think about what a reviewer actually says. Not that the report is wrong. That revenue is flagged as material, and it is not, because the contract slipped a week and landed in March. The report is fine. One judgement inside it is not. There was no way to record that.

props.sparkLine: The report is fine. That number is not.

layers.title: Approve
layers.sub: accepts everything, including the bit you think is wrong

layers.title: Request changes
layers.sub: sends the whole report back over one figure

layers.title: The real case
layers.sub: accept the report, reject one finding inside it

props.caption: The third one is what reviewers actually do, and it had nowhere to go.

beats.narration_text: Left unrecorded, that correction goes into an email, or somebody's memory, and it is gone by the next close. And the tempting fix is far worse: let the reviewer edit the number. Do that and you destroy the only record that the machine and the human ever disagreed.

show.event: the editing chip lands last, in terracotta

items: Into a comment on a closed ticket
Into the number itself, erasing both sides
props.caption: The last one looks like a fix and is the most destructive.

beats.narration_text: So the rule I settled on is that the log records the disagreement and resolves nothing. Both positions survive. The engine's number stays exactly as the engine computed it, and the reviewer's objection sits next to it with a name on it.

props.title: Record It, Do Not Settle It
props.body: Both positions survive. The engine's number is untouched and the objection sits beside it with a name on it.

beats.narration_text: Which needs one rule enforced in code. The reviewer is not allowed to restate the engine's value in their own record. If they try, it is refused. The engine's number is copied from the run itself, so there is exactly one source for it and no opportunity to quietly adjust it on the way past.

props.title: disagreement.py — one source for the number
props.code:
# A reviewer may not restate the engine's number as their own. Both sides
# are kept verbatim, and the engine's value is copied from the run, never
# from the record.
if "engine_value" in record:
    raise DisagreementError(
        "disagreement must not restate engine_value; it is read from the run"
    )

beats.narration_text: Run against the real February investigation it looks like this. A named controller takes a position on revenue, with a stated reason. And on the line underneath, the engine's finding, unchanged. Minus ninety thousand, exactly as computed, sitting next to somebody saying they do not think it matters.

show.event: the reviewer and position write on
the unchanged engine finding lands in terracotta

props.artifactHeading: Both positions, on the same screen
artifactLines: basis      the contract slipped a week and settled in March

beats.narration_text: Now the test that stops it being a comment box. You can only disagree with something the engine actually said. Try to object to marketing, which this run never reported on, and it refuses and tells you why. A disagreement that is not anchored to a specific finding cannot be checked by anybody later.

show.event: the quoted refusal types on as the serif title

props.title: “The Engine Said Nothing About It”
props.body: Objecting to marketing, which this run never reported on, is refused — and the refusal says why. A disagreement nobody can tie to a specific finding cannot be checked by anybody later.

beats.narration_text: Three more refusals hold it together. The agent cannot file a disagreement, because a system objecting to itself is not review. A reason under twenty characters is not a reason. And the log is bound to the run's hash, so if the investigation is rerun the log detaches rather than quietly pointing at findings that no longer exist.

show.event: 'Not a detached log' lands in terracotta

layers.title: Not a detached log

props.caption: Each one is a refusal to write, never a warning on the report.

beats.narration_text: And two reviewers may disagree with the same finding and both entries stand. That is deliberate. The log is the history of an argument, not a vote, and a system that tallied disagreements into a verdict would be making exactly the judgement it has no business making.

show.event: the two objections and the engine value light in order

props.destTitle: holds all three and decides between none of them
props.arcCaption: nothing is tallied, nothing is adopted

beats.narration_text: The honest limit is that nothing downstream reads this yet. A recorded disagreement changes no number and blocks no report on its own. What it does is make the argument survive the week it happened in, which is more than an email does.

props.title: It Resolves Nothing
props.body: A recorded disagreement changes no number and blocks no report by itself. It makes the argument survive the week it happened in.

beats.narration_text: So, the verdict. The review gate could approve, request changes, or block, and none of those fit the case reviewers hit most often: the report is fine, that one number is not. Disagreements are now recorded beside the finding they dispute. The engine's value is copied from the run and a record that tries to restate it is refused, so there is one source for the number and no chance to adjust it in passing. You can only object to something the engine actually said. The agent cannot object at all. And two people may disagree with the same figure, because this is the history of an argument and not a vote.

show.event: the 'agent cannot file one' line holds in terracotta

props.artifactHeading: Both sides survive, neither one wins
artifactLines: Approve, request changes and block never fit the real case: accept the report, reject one finding.
Disagreements sit beside the finding. The engine's number is copied from the run, never restated.
You may only object to something the engine actually reported. Unanchored objections are refused.
The agent cannot file one. A system objecting to itself is not review.
Two reviewers may disagree with the same figure. It is a history, not a vote.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here is the prompt. Think about the last time you overrode something a tool told you. Tell me where that correction is recorded now, who could find it in six months, and what would happen if the tool produced the same output again next week. Then tell me whether anything in your system would notice. Run that honestly. Most overrides are recorded nowhere, which means the same argument gets had again from scratch.

props.command: Think about the last time you overrode something a tool told you. Where is that correction recorded now, who could find it in six months, and what happens if the tool produces the same output next week? Would anything in the system notice?
output: Most overrides are recorded nowhere, so the same argument gets had again from scratch.
If nothing would notice, the override was advice, not a decision.

beats.narration_text: That was the reviewer disagreement log for the Mycroft Finance Investigator. The code and the tests are in pull request seventeen. Adwait Changan, for Humanitarians AI.
